descriptionChirho: The proper noun אֶסְתֵּר (Esther), the Persian name (possibly from Old Persian 'stara', star, or the goddess Ishtar) of Hadassah, the Jewish queen of Persia and protagonist of the Book of Esther. All 55 occurrences appear exclusively in the Book of Esther and render consistently across languages: eng 'Esther', spa 'Ester', hin 'एस्तेर', arb 'أَسْتِيرُ/أَسْتِيرَ', kor '에스더', swa 'Esta'. The two clusters differ only in prefixed prepositions: S83618 (54x) includes bare, lamed-prefixed, and waw-conjunction forms, while S83621 (1x) has the min-preposition ('from Esther'). These are grammatical variations, not semantic distinctions.
